topic: The week before the Suneung (2027 CSAT, Thu 2026-11-19, 551,864 applicants, MOE/KICE 2026-09-08): yeot and chapssaltteok gifts (stick = pass), fork (jjikda = pick) and toilet paper (pulda = solve), no seaweed soup (slip = fail), parents praying at Jogyesa/Bongeunsa, juniors cheering at the gates, students would rather get practical gifts
title: In Korea, the Week Before the Big Exam Has Its Own Menu

slides.headline: In Korea, the week before the big exam has **its own menu.**
slides.note: Sticky taffy, rice cakes, and no seaweed soup.

slides.headline: **Sticky** taffy
slides.body: Before the Suneung (수능), Korea's university entrance exam, people give students yeot, a hard sticky taffy. In Korean, "to stick" also means to get into a school.

slides.headline: Rice cakes **that cling**
slides.body: Chapssaltteok, chewy rice cakes made of sticky rice, carry the same wish. Every November, shops stack gift boxes of both by the door.

slides.headline: A fork and **toilet paper**
slides.body: The Korean word for stabbing with a fork also means picking an answer. The word for unrolling also means solving a problem. So both make a good-luck gift.

slides.headline: **No** seaweed soup
slides.body: Seaweed is slippery, and "to slip" in Korean also means to fail a test. Many families keep miyeokguk (미역국), the usual birthday soup, off the table until the exam is over.

slides.headline: Parents **pray**
slides.body: At Seoul temples like Jogyesa and Bongeunsa, parents light candles and bow, some every day for 100 days. Churches and cathedrals hold services too.

slides.headline: Juniors **at the gate**
slides.body: On exam morning, younger students wait outside the test sites before dawn with signs and cheers. Teachers and even education officials join them.

slides.headline: Students signed up **for this year's exam**
slides.body: The test is on Thursday, November 19. More than 170,000 of them have already finished high school and are trying again.

slides.headline: What students **really want**
slides.body: In one survey, about a third of students named taffy and rice cakes as the gift they least wanted. Many would rather get a gift card or a warm drink.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.
slides.graphic: A quiet Seoul classroom desk at night with a lamp, blurred behind the text.

caption:
Next Thursday, about 550,000 students in Korea sit the university entrance exam. This week, they get sticky taffy, rice cakes, forks and toilet paper, and nobody serves them seaweed soup.

Every gift is a pun on passing.

What do people in your country do for luck before a big exam?
reply: One more thing: after the exam, many shops and restaurants give students a discount if they show their exam ticket. What would you buy first?
fact_check: 1·8장: 2027학년도 수능 2026-11-19(목), 응시원서 551,864명, 졸업생 약 17.4만명(평가원 2026-09-08 발표, 뉴시스·SBS Biz·유가크루 정리).
2·3장: 엿·찹쌀떡 = 붙으라는 기원, 학력고사 시절부터 기본 선물(시대에듀·YTN).
4장: 포크(잘 찍어라)·휴지(잘 풀어라), 1993년 수능 도입 이후 등장(YTN 2024-11).
5장: 미역국 = 미끄러짐 연상 미신, AFP 보도(헤럴드경제 2025-11-13).
6장: 조계사 초 공양·봉은사 수능 기도, 백일기도, 성당·교회 기도회(뉴시스 2025-11-12·13).
7장: 고사장 앞 후배 응원, 서울시교육감 팻말 응원(헤럴드경제 2025-11-12).
reply: 수험표 할인은 매년 업체별 행사, 확정 목록 아님(일반 안내).
